request.idea: An AI platform that helps college students in India discover relevant internships and manage applications.

startup.normalizedDescription: A student-facing platform that uses AI to find relevant internships, explain matches, and organize the application workflow for college students in India.
startup.initialUserHypothesis: College students who actively search and apply for internships
startup.initialBuyerHypothesis: Students may buy optional application support; universities are an alternative institutional buyer requiring validation.
startup.initialBusinessTypeHypothesis: B2C freemium or B2B2C institutional subscription requires validation
startup.valueProposition: Help students find relevant internships faster, understand why each role fits, and reduce repetitive application work.
coreWorkflow: Set internship preferences and upload a profile
Receive ranked internship matches with explanations
startup.confidenceReason: The user explicitly supplied the geography, audience, and main outcome; buyer and monetization choices remain hypotheses.

executiveSummary.summary: Available mock evidence supports a recurring student problem around fragmented internship discovery, repeated application work, and deadline tracking. A transparent matching and tracking workflow appears worth testing, but market sizing is disputed, direct willingness-to-pay evidence is weak, institutional buying evidence is limited, and long-term listing access remains unresolved. The opportunity is promising under the V1 rubric, with a provisional score of 67 and Medium confidence; the next decision should come from customer and buyer experiments rather than a broad product build.

dimensions.confidenceReason: The concierge scope is clear, but half of the fixed input weight is unavailable because critical data, privacy, and integration dependencies were not verified.
dimensions.calculationExplanation: Assessed inputs average to 100 across 50% weighted coverage. The V1 40–59% coverage rule caps the dimension at 65, so the emitted score is 65.

opportunityScore.confidenceReason: Problem evidence is comparatively strong, but Market Potential, Monetization Potential, and Execution Feasibility contain material conflicts or gaps. The weighted confidence indicator is 0.80, and two Low-confidence dimensions with 15% weights prevent a High label.

coverageSummary.statusExplanation: All seven dimensions are assessed, but Execution Feasibility has 50% weighted coverage and is capped at 65; the overall score is therefore Provisional.

opportunityScore.calculationExplanation: The overall score is the fixed weighted sum: 16.20 + 10.35 + 9.45 + 6.00 + 9.90 + 4.90 + 9.75 = 66.55, rounded once to 67. No weights were redistributed.

businessModel.recommendationRationale: Validate the institutional subscription first because it aligns with an existing career-services workflow and avoids charging students for basic discovery. This is a test priority, not proof that universities will buy.
businessModel.comparisonSummary: Freemium offers the simplest student adoption path but has weak direct payment evidence. Institutional subscription has limited but relevant budget evidence and a clearer service owner, while adding procurement complexity. Referral revenue has comparable precedent but creates trust and two-sided-market risks that are unnecessary for the first validation cycle.
businessModel.confidenceReason: Comparable models and limited budget signals exist, but neither direct student payment nor institutional purchase intent has been validated for this product.

validationExperiments.title: Concierge explained-shortlist test
validationExperiments.hypothesis: Active internship seekers will act on a small curated shortlist more often when each opportunity includes a clear fit explanation.
validationExperiments.artifactOrStimulus: A manually prepared shortlist of five to ten verified internships with structured match reasons and source links.
procedure: Recruit active applicants with near-term internship goals.
Collect preferences and current search methods.
Deliver one explained shortlist.
Observe saves, rejections, applications, and explanation feedback for seven days.

metric.name: Qualified shortlist action rate
metric.definition: Share of shortlist items saved, prioritized, or applied to within seven days.
metric.collectionMethod: Instrumented link and follow-up activity log.
metric.caveat: A small concierge sample measures behavior direction, not market-wide conversion.

outcomeCriteria.supportCriteria: Participants act on at least 30% of delivered items and most can explain why selected matches fit.
outcomeCriteria.weakenCriteria: Participants act on fewer than 10% of items or report that explanations do not affect decisions.
inconclusiveConditions: Listings are stale, participants are not actively applying, or follow-up data is missing.
outcomeCriteria.decisionRuleRationale: Behavior on actual opportunities is more informative than stated enthusiasm.

validationExperiments.expectedLearning: Whether relevance and explanation produce real shortlist actions and which explanation details matter.
validationExperiments.priorityRationale: Tests the central value proposition and the most important adoption risk with minimal software.

validationExperiments.title: Application-workflow diary study
validationExperiments.hypothesis: Active applicants repeatedly lose time to portal switching, data re-entry, and manual deadline tracking across a two-week period.
validationExperiments.artifactOrStimulus: A simple daily log for searches, applications, re-entry, tracking actions, and missed deadlines.
procedure: Recruit students currently planning at least three applications.
Collect a baseline workflow map.
Record actions and time for fourteen days.
Review repeated friction and exceptions in a closing interview.

metric.name: Repeated-friction incidence
metric.definition: Number of participants experiencing each friction on at least three separate days.
metric.collectionMethod: Daily diary plus closing interview verification.
metric.caveat: Self-recorded time can be imprecise and participation may change behavior.

outcomeCriteria.supportCriteria: A majority experience at least one target friction on three or more days and can show the workaround used.
outcomeCriteria.weakenCriteria: Most complete applications through one satisfactory workflow with little repeated coordination.
inconclusiveConditions: Participants submit too few applications or diary completion is poor.
outcomeCriteria.decisionRuleRationale: Repeated observed behavior establishes frequency more reliably than one-time recall.

validationExperiments.expectedLearning: Which workflow step deserves the MVP focus and whether the five-hour estimate is plausible.
validationExperiments.priorityRationale: Improves problem and customer evidence while preventing overbuilding around an infrequent pain.

validationExperiments.title: Student premium-value test
validationExperiments.hypothesis: After receiving useful free matching, some active applicants will commit to paying for a specific application-support outcome rather than for basic discovery.
validationExperiments.artifactOrStimulus: A clear premium offer for one defined service, such as a tailored application pack review, shown after the free shortlist.
procedure: Complete the free shortlist experience.
Present the same premium outcome and fulfillment terms to each participant.
Ask for a refundable deposit or scheduled paid pilot commitment.
Interview acceptors and decliners about the decision.

metric.name: Verified payment commitment
metric.definition: Count and share of eligible participants making the defined deposit or paid-pilot commitment.
metric.collectionMethod: Payment or signed commitment record, not survey intent.
metric.caveat: One service and one sample do not establish a final price or long-term retention.

outcomeCriteria.supportCriteria: At least three participants or 15% of the eligible sample make the defined commitment, whichever threshold is harder.
outcomeCriteria.weakenCriteria: No participant commits despite demonstrated free value and a clearly understood offer.
inconclusiveConditions: Participants did not value the free shortlist, the offer was misunderstood, or payment handling failed.
outcomeCriteria.decisionRuleRationale: A behavioral commitment is stronger than stated willingness to pay.

validationExperiments.expectedLearning: Whether any student-paid wedge deserves further pricing research and what outcome motivates payment.
validationExperiments.priorityRationale: Direct payment evidence is absent and Monetization Potential is the weakest score dimension.

validationExperiments.title: University buyer interviews and pilot ask
validationExperiments.hypothesis: Career-services teams will consider sponsoring a small cohort pilot when it reduces manual curation or improves observable student engagement.
validationExperiments.artifactOrStimulus: A one-page cohort-pilot proposal with workflow, student outcome, staff responsibility, privacy boundary, and a concrete sponsorship ask.
procedure: Interview career-services staff about current workflow and budget owner.
Map procurement and privacy requirements.
Present the pilot proposal only after problem discovery.
Record introductions, follow-up actions, and commitment level.

metric.name: Qualified institutional commitment
metric.definition: Number of interviewees who identify a budget owner and agree to a next-step pilot review, letter of intent, or paid/sponsored pilot discussion.
metric.collectionMethod: Documented follow-up action and named decision process.
metric.caveat: Meeting interest is not a purchase; require a concrete next action.

outcomeCriteria.supportCriteria: At least two institutions identify a plausible budget owner and agree to a defined pilot next step.
outcomeCriteria.weakenCriteria: Most report no owned problem, no budget path, or requirements that exceed MVP scope.
inconclusiveConditions: Interviewees lack decision context or the pilot outcome is too vague.
outcomeCriteria.decisionRuleRationale: The test must reveal procurement reality as well as interest.

validationExperiments.expectedLearning: Whether the recommended institutional model has a real buyer, what outcome matters, and how long procurement may take.
validationExperiments.priorityRationale: The recommended business-model candidate rests on limited buyer evidence.

validationExperiments.title: Internship data-supply feasibility audit
validationExperiments.hypothesis: A narrow pilot can maintain a sufficiently fresh and relevant listing set using permitted sources and manual verification.
validationExperiments.artifactOrStimulus: A two-week source register tracking permission, freshness, duplication, coverage, and manual processing time.
procedure: Select a narrow role and geography boundary.
Identify permitted sources and access conditions.
Collect and deduplicate listings daily for two weeks.
Measure freshness, relevant coverage, and researcher time.

metric.name: Verified listing coverage and maintenance effort
metric.definition: Count of unique eligible fresh listings and manual hours required per weekly shortlist.
metric.collectionMethod: Source register and timestamped operations log.
metric.caveat: A narrow audit establishes pilot feasibility, not nationwide scale.

outcomeCriteria.supportCriteria: The team can maintain enough fresh eligible listings for each participant shortlist within the pilot's manual time budget.
outcomeCriteria.weakenCriteria: Permitted sources provide too few listings or maintenance effort makes the pilot impractical.
inconclusiveConditions: The chosen role or geography is unrepresentative or source permissions remain ambiguous.
outcomeCriteria.decisionRuleRationale: This separates customer-value validation from an unverified scaling assumption while still checking that the pilot can operate.

validationExperiments.expectedLearning: Whether manual supply supports the MVP and which access strategy needs deeper research.
validationExperiments.priorityRationale: A Critical data risk and two unavailable execution inputs depend on this question.

recommendation.summary: Continue investigating InternPath AI through a concierge student pilot, a university buyer test, and a data-supply audit before building a broad automated platform.
recommendation.whyThisVerdict: The deterministic score is 67 with a Promising band because problem, customer, and competitive signals are favorable. The score is Provisional and confidence is Medium because market estimates conflict, monetization evidence is indirect, and half of the execution inputs are unavailable.

scoreBasis.interpretation: The score supports continued investigation, while the coverage cap and Low-confidence dimensions make focused validation more appropriate than significant product investment.

strongestSignals.statement: Students repeatedly use fragmented search and tracking workflows.
strongestSignals.whyItMatters: The MVP targets an observable recurring behavior rather than interest alone.

strongestSignals.statement: Transparent match explanations connect a supported trust need to incomplete direct-competitor coverage.
strongestSignals.whyItMatters: It supplies a specific, testable differentiation hypothesis.

strongestSignals.statement: A concierge workflow can test the core value without first building a marketplace or automated ingestion system.
strongestSignals.whyItMatters: It reduces the cost of learning before technical commitments.

biggestConcerns.statement: A durable and permitted internship-listing supply has not been verified.
biggestConcerns.whyItMatters: Insufficient supply could block match quality and scale.

biggestConcerns.statement: Direct willingness-to-pay evidence for this product is absent.
biggestConcerns.whyItMatters: Usage may not produce a sustainable payer or revenue model.

biggestConcerns.statement: The mock market population sources use conflicting inclusion boundaries.
biggestConcerns.whyItMatters: Market-scale confidence is lower than the available point estimates imply.

criticalUnknowns.question: Will explained shortlists change real student shortlist and application behavior?
criticalUnknowns.whyDecisionChanging: A negative result would weaken the core user value and differentiation hypotheses.

criticalUnknowns.question: Will students or university career-services teams make a concrete payment or pilot commitment?
criticalUnknowns.whyDecisionChanging: The answer determines which buyer path, if any, deserves further work.

criticalUnknowns.question: Can the pilot maintain enough fresh, permitted listings within a practical operating budget?
criticalUnknowns.whyDecisionChanging: A negative result could make the current product scope infeasible or require a narrower source strategy.

nextSteps.statement: Run the concierge explained-shortlist experiment with active internship applicants.
nextSteps.whyNow: It tests the central value and adoption behavior before product automation.

nextSteps.statement: Complete the two-week data-supply feasibility audit for one narrow role and geography.
nextSteps.whyNow: It addresses the main execution blocker and the score's coverage cap.

nextSteps.statement: Interview university career-services buyers and make a concrete cohort-pilot ask.
nextSteps.whyNow: The recommended business-model candidate has only limited buyer evidence.

nextSteps.statement: Test a specific premium student outcome after participants experience the free shortlist.
nextSteps.whyNow: This creates direct payment evidence without confusing discovery interest with willingness to pay.

nextSteps.statement: Defer automated submission, employer marketplace features, and predictive acceptance scoring.
nextSteps.whyNow: They add dependencies and claims that are unnecessary for the current learning goals.

recommendation.confidenceReason: Several sections align on a testable student workflow, but buyer identity, direct payment, market boundaries, and scalable listing access remain decision-changing unknowns.

evidence.claim: In the mock student workflow survey, 68% of active internship seekers used three or more discovery channels in the prior month.
evidence.supportingText: 68% reported using at least three portals, college channels, or messaging groups.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock survey result for the target segment; sampling is illustrative and limited.

evidence.claim: In the mock survey, 54% of recent applicants reported re-entering similar profile information in multiple application workflows.
evidence.supportingText: 54% selected repeated entry of education or skill details as a recurring task.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock survey result, with limited sample representativeness.

evidence.claim: The mock community digest contains repeated reports of students missing deadlines or losing application status across portals and messaging groups.
evidence.supportingText: Students described spreadsheets, bookmarks, and chat reminders that became difficult to maintain.
evidence.confidenceReason: Useful direct language from a mock community source, but not representative of all students.

evidence.claim: The mock placement-office brief reports that portals and campus support already help many students discover internships.
evidence.supportingText: Staff described existing portal lists, employer relationships, and counseling as common supports.
evidence.confidenceReason: Relevant institutional mock source that directly describes existing alternatives.

evidence.claim: Some mock college career cells use spreadsheets and messaging groups to distribute opportunities and monitor student responses.
evidence.supportingText: Processes varied by institution and frequently relied on manual coordination.
evidence.confidenceReason: Two mock institutional sources support the process pattern, but institutions vary.

evidence.claim: In the mock student payment poll, 18% reported paying for an adjacent resume review, mentoring, or career-support service during the prior year.
evidence.supportingText: 18% reported at least one paid adjacent career-support purchase.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock behavior report, but adjacent services may not transfer to this product.

evidence.claim: In the same mock poll, 72% expected internship discovery and basic listing access to be free.
evidence.supportingText: 72% selected free as the expected price for basic discovery.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock result relevant to basic discovery, but not to all premium outcomes.

evidence.claim: In the mock student poll, 61% preferred internship recommendations that included a reason for the match.
evidence.supportingText: 61% selected explained recommendations over unexplained rankings.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock preference evidence; it does not prove behavior change.

evidence.claim: PathPilot describes personalized internship discovery and application tracking for students.
evidence.supportingText: The mock homepage presents matching and tracking as its main student workflow.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct official mock company source, suitable for current self-described positioning.

evidence.claim: PathPilot documents profile-based personalized matching.
evidence.supportingText: Matches use skills, location, schedule, and interests.
evidence.confidenceReason: Explicit official mock feature description.

evidence.claim: PathPilot provides a short fit label, but the mock page does not document detailed match explanations.
evidence.supportingText: A fit label is shown without a documented factor-by-factor rationale.
evidence.confidenceReason: The partial capability is visible; absence of further detail is not proof that no other explanation exists.

evidence.claim: PathPilot documents an in-product application status tracker.
evidence.supportingText: Users can save roles and update application status.
evidence.confidenceReason: Explicit official mock feature description.

evidence.claim: PathPilot lists resume templates but does not document role-specific resume tailoring.
evidence.supportingText: Template library included with student plans.
evidence.confidenceReason: Templates are explicit; broader support remains unverified.

evidence.claim: PathPilot lists a free student plan and a Plus plan at INR 299 per month.
evidence.supportingText: Free: INR 0; Plus: INR 299/month.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct current mock pricing page.

evidence.claim: InternBridge describes internship listings, assisted applications, and status tracking for Indian students.
evidence.supportingText: The mock homepage emphasizes listings and application assistance.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct official mock company source.

evidence.claim: InternBridge supports filters and saved preferences but explicitly does not provide match reasoning.
evidence.supportingText: Results are filter-based; the help page states that no match rationale is generated.
evidence.confidenceReason: The mock official source directly describes both behaviors.

evidence.claim: InternBridge supports assisted application submission for covered listings.
evidence.supportingText: Apply Assist submits supported applications after student review.
evidence.confidenceReason: Explicit official mock feature description.

evidence.claim: InternBridge documents an application status board.
evidence.supportingText: The student dashboard includes saved opportunities and application status.
evidence.confidenceReason: Explicit official mock feature description.

evidence.claim: InternBridge lists free browsing and an Apply Assist plan at INR 499 per month.
evidence.supportingText: Browse: free; Apply Assist: INR 499/month.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct current mock pricing page.

evidence.claim: CareerOrbit serves broad early-career discovery and redirects applications to employer sites without tracking them.
evidence.supportingText: Applications take place externally and are not stored in the candidate dashboard.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct official mock source.

evidence.claim: CareerOrbit documents profile-based early-career opportunity recommendations.
evidence.supportingText: Recommendations use profile and role preferences.
evidence.confidenceReason: Explicit official mock product statement.

evidence.claim: CareerOrbit documents candidate resume review tools.
evidence.supportingText: Candidate tools include resume checks and revision prompts.
evidence.confidenceReason: Explicit official mock product statement.

evidence.claim: CareerOrbit states that it earns referral fees from selected employer and service partners.
evidence.supportingText: The mock disclosure lists referral revenue for selected partner actions.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct official mock disclosure, appropriate for the company's stated revenue model.

evidence.claim: The mock campus-career guide describes manual role recommendations by career-services staff.
evidence.supportingText: Career cells may recommend roles to students using local employer knowledge.
evidence.confidenceReason: Relevant mock institutional source, but it summarizes heterogeneous colleges.

evidence.claim: The mock campus-career guide describes counselors explaining why selected roles may fit a student.
evidence.supportingText: Some career cells offer individual guidance about eligibility and fit.
evidence.confidenceReason: The mock guide documents the practice but says delivery varies by institution.

evidence.claim: The mock campus-career guide describes some career cells using spreadsheets or forms to track student applications.
evidence.supportingText: Tracking practices include shared spreadsheets and forms at some institutions.
evidence.confidenceReason: The workflow is documented, but it is not standardized across institutions.

evidence.claim: The mock campus-career guide does not establish a consistent application-submission function across institutions.
evidence.supportingText: The guide describes distribution and support but no standard cross-institution submission workflow.
evidence.confidenceReason: Absence from one cross-institution guide supports Not confirmed, not a claim that the capability never exists.

evidence.claim: The mock campus-career guide lists resume workshops and review support among common career-cell services.
evidence.supportingText: Resume workshops and individual reviews are listed as common student services.
evidence.confidenceReason: The mock guide explicitly lists the service category.

evidence.claim: The mock campus-career guide reports that service coverage and workflow implementation vary across colleges.
evidence.supportingText: Staff capacity, employer access, and tracking processes differ by institution.
evidence.confidenceReason: The mock guide summarizes multiple institutions but does not measure every college.

evidence.claim: The mock education statistics release reports 8 million students within its defined internship-relevant undergraduate population.
evidence.supportingText: 8.0 million students met the release's age, enrolment, and program filters.
evidence.confidenceReason: Mock government-style source with a clear method, but its boundary conflicts with another mock estimate.

evidence.claim: The mock internship-seeking poll reports that 40% of surveyed college students were actively seeking an internship.
evidence.supportingText: 40% were searching or applying during the survey period.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock survey result, with uncertain applicability to the full population.

evidence.claim: The mock recruitment trend report shows 12% year-over-year growth in students using digital internship-discovery channels.
evidence.supportingText: Digital-channel participation increased 12% from 2025 to 2026 in the mock panel.
evidence.confidenceReason: Current and geography-relevant mock research, but only one origin supports the trend.

evidence.claim: A second mock market memo estimates 5 million internship-relevant college students using a narrower program and urban-access boundary.
evidence.supportingText: The memo reports 5.0 million after excluding several program types and low-connectivity regions.
evidence.confidenceReason: The mock industry memo describes its narrower boundary but provides less transparent methodology.

evidence.claim: In a mock brief covering six university career-services interviews, three teams reported an existing budget category for employability or placement software.
evidence.supportingText: Three of six teams identified a relevant software budget, but no team evaluated InternPath AI.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock buyer evidence, but the sample is small and product-specific purchase intent was not tested.

evidence.claim: Active applicants in the mock workflow survey reported a median of five hours per week spent searching, checking fit, and organizing internship applications.
evidence.supportingText: Median self-reported weekly workflow time was five hours among active applicants.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock self-report; recall error and active-applicant selection may affect the value.

evidence.claim: The mock AI trust study reports that students want to understand and verify why career recommendations were made.
evidence.supportingText: Participants asked for visible recommendation factors and source details before acting.
evidence.confidenceReason: Direct mock study finding relevant to recommendation trust, though not specific to internship applications.

evidence.claim: The derived serviceable student population is 3.2 million under the selected mock boundary.
evidence.analysisMethod: Multiply 8,000,000 eligible students by the 40% active internship-seeking share: 8,000,000 × 0.40 = 3,200,000.
evidence.confidenceReason: The arithmetic is deterministic, but population disagreement and survey applicability reduce confidence.

evidence.claim: The median of the two verified mock direct-competitor premium prices is INR 399 per month.
evidence.confidenceReason: Calculation is exact for the two verified prices, but the sample is too small to establish a market price.

evidence.claim: Zero of the two verified direct competitors have Confirmed detailed match explanations under the matrix inclusion rule.
evidence.analysisMethod: Count direct competitors with status Confirmed for detailed match explanations; Partial and Confirmed absent do not enter the numerator.
evidence.confidenceReason: Deterministic for the verified direct set; broader competitor coverage is incomplete.

evidence.claim: A complementary cross-source shortlist and tracker may reduce observed workflow fragmentation without requiring students to replace existing portals.
evidence.analysisMethod: Synthesize repeated customer workarounds with evidence that existing portals remain useful; frame the product as a complementary workflow hypothesis.
evidence.confidenceReason: The inference follows observed behavior and counter-evidence but has not been tested with a product.

evidence.claim: Transparent match explanations may be a meaningful differentiation hypothesis for active student applicants.
evidence.analysisMethod: Connect customer explanation preference and trust evidence to the verified direct-competitor feature pattern.
evidence.confidenceReason: The need and competitor pattern align, but preference has not been shown to change behavior.

evidence.claim: University career-services teams are a plausible buyer to validate because some own related workflows and adjacent software budgets.
evidence.analysisMethod: Connect observed workflow ownership to limited adjacent budget evidence; retain buyer status as uncertain.
evidence.confidenceReason: The mock sample is small and no product-specific purchase intent exists.

evidence.claim: Meaningful student workflow fragmentation remains even though portals and placement cells already provide useful alternatives.
evidence.analysisMethod: Reconcile observed multi-channel behavior with evidence that current alternatives solve parts of discovery and support.
evidence.confidenceReason: The sources agree that both fragmentation and partial solutions exist.

assumptions.statement: The mock online student samples are directionally useful for an initial segment of English-speaking, digitally active Indian college students.
assumptions.reason: The available mock sources do not establish representativeness across all colleges, languages, regions, or access levels.
assumptions.validationSuggestion: Recruit a deliberately varied interview and diary-study sample across college types, regions, and study years.

assumptions.statement: The 40% internship-seeking share can be applied to the 8 million sourced population for the illustrative SAM calculation.
assumptions.reason: The two sources use similar but not proven-identical population boundaries.
assumptions.validationSuggestion: Align denominator definitions and obtain a geography- and enrolment-matched seeking rate.

assumptions.statement: Students may use free discovery and consider paying for a distinct premium application-support outcome.
assumptions.reason: Comparable plans and adjacent payment behavior exist, but direct product payment behavior has not been tested.
assumptions.validationSuggestion: Run exp_003 with a concrete outcome and behavioral payment commitment.

assumptions.statement: University career-services teams could be an initial institutional buyer or pilot sponsor.
assumptions.reason: They own a related workflow and some report adjacent budgets, but product-specific authority and intent are unknown.
assumptions.validationSuggestion: Run exp_004 to identify budget owners, requirements, and concrete pilot commitments.

assumptions.statement: Publicly accessible mock competitor pages reflect the capabilities available to typical Indian student users at the time of access.
assumptions.reason: The research did not use product accounts or independent feature testing.
assumptions.validationSuggestion: Verify critical competitor capabilities through product trials or current demos before product positioning decisions.

assumptions.statement: A researcher can manually source and verify enough permitted listings to operate a narrow concierge MVP.
assumptions.reason: A scalable access path is unknown, but a manual pilot needs a temporary supply approach.
assumptions.validationSuggestion: Run exp_005 and set an explicit listing-coverage and researcher-time budget.

assumptions.statement: Employers may benefit indirectly if students receive more relevant opportunities and prepare applications more effectively.
assumptions.reason: The MVP focuses on students and career-services buyers, so employer outcomes were not directly researched.
assumptions.validationSuggestion: Revisit employer benefits only if an employer-facing or referral model becomes an active validation priority.

limitations.statement: This file is a fictional mock fixture for interface development; none of its companies, sources, values, or research findings should be treated as real-world evidence.
limitations.reason: The fixture is designed to exercise the canonical contract and dashboard states safely.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Replace the mock fixture only after the frontend contract is stable and real n8n research stages are implemented.

limitations.statement: Student survey and community evidence may overrepresent digitally active and highly motivated internship seekers.
limitations.reason: The mock samples do not establish national representativeness.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Recruit a varied primary-research sample and report segment differences.

limitations.statement: Market population sources conflict because they use different program, enrolment, and access boundaries.
limitations.reason: The 8 million and 5 million figures are not directly comparable and must not be averaged.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Choose one explicit market boundary and obtain matched population and internship-seeking inputs.

limitations.statement: Only four competitor or substitute records were verified; one candidate was inaccessible, two feature-matrix cells are Unknown, and two are Not confirmed.
limitations.reason: Public-page research cannot establish complete market or capability coverage.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Verify the inaccessible candidate and test critical capabilities inside current products.

limitations.statement: No reliable direct willingness-to-pay evidence exists for InternPath AI or its proposed premium outcomes.
limitations.reason: Adjacent purchases, stated preferences, and competitor prices do not prove product-specific payment behavior.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Run exp_003 using a real payment or deposit commitment after participants experience the free value.

limitations.statement: Institutional buyer evidence covers only six mock career-services interviews and does not establish authority, procurement timing, or product-specific intent.
limitations.reason: Budget adjacency is weaker than a purchase commitment.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Run exp_004 and document budget owner, decision process, requirements, and a concrete next action.

limitations.statement: The research did not verify durable listing permissions, source access, integration feasibility, privacy requirements, or production AI quality.
limitations.reason: The current specification is research-focused and has no production dependency audit.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Run exp_005 and a focused privacy, terms, integration, and model-quality review before automation.

limitations.statement: No recommended validation experiment has been executed, so SOM, activation, retention, conversion, and outcome thresholds remain unavailable.
limitations.reason: Recommended experiments are plans, not evidence.
limitations.recommendedFollowUp: Execute the prioritized experiments and add their results as new observed evidence in a future report version.
